title: Fail instead of skip when the supervised rehearsals are required, keep greg rehearse bodies below the founder tier, and run the build-frontier gates on every pull request
problem: Three gaps at base 44b3df96 (#236's head). (1) Both supervised rehearsal modules skip when supervisord is not on PATH. With the default PATH (supervisord only in /home/user/venv311/bin) they report '4 skipped' and exit 0, so the build frontier's N1/N2 count can rest on a skip. (2) Any holder of an enrolled key can sign FOUNDER_TIER directly (greg/metrics.py says so). A `greg rehearse` body keeps its throwaway key on disk with no passphrase. A probe on the base (rehearsal body, self-signed FOUNDER_TIER, then a MISSION, VEPMC rows stubbed) read tier FOUNDER_TIER, achieved ['N0', 'N1'], active N2. That is the failure evidence INTENT-20261030-BUILD-BEFORE-DEVICE-RUN names: 'a test key or rehearsal that moves VEPMC or greg path N1'. (3) No workflow ran #236's path-predicate mutation gate.

INTENT-20261028-OPUS-MAXIMUS-REISSUE (sections 56 reality ladder, 64 external reality is final judge, 70 and 73)

baseline: 44b3df96: test_greg_chromebook_rehearsal.py and test_greg_vepmc_path.py carry skipif marks on shutil.which('supervisord'). `greg rehearse` creates a body, enrolls an unprotected throwaway key and signs MISSIONs whose founder_expression opens with '[REHEARSAL]'. metrics.founder_tier admits any MISSION signed by the enrolled founder key after that key signed FOUNDER_TIER. scripts/ci/check_path_predicate_mutants.py exists, and no workflow runs it.

alternatives.name: Proposed: fail-closed helper, rehearsal mark plus ledger label read, a build-frontier workflow and a mutant gate
alternatives.description: tests/supervisor_requirement.py fails each supervised rehearsal test with one message under GREG_REQUIRE_SUPERVISOR=1, and skips otherwise; both modules call it from an autouse fixture. `greg rehearse` writes a 'rehearsal' mark into body.json before the throwaway key is enrolled. metrics.rehearsal_body reads the mark or an accepted MISSION whose signed founder_expression opens with rehearsal.LABEL, and founder_tier holds every mission of such a body at STRUCTURAL_CANDIDATE. tier_status and Mission Control's Proof row say why. .github/workflows/build-frontier.yml runs both mutation gates and the rehearsals under the requirement on every pull request. 29 mutants pin it.
advantages: With GREG_REQUIRE_SUPERVISOR=1 and no supervisord, the run gives 4 setup errors with the exact message and exits 1, instead of '4 skipped' and exit 0
A self-attested rehearsal body stays STRUCTURAL_CANDIDATE and achieved stays ['N0'], including a body made by the base's code
Read side only: greg/body.py, greg/console.py, conftest.py and canonical-ci.yml are not edited, so no overlap with #221, #235, #233 or the Canonical CI PRs
Every safeguard has a caught mutant (29/29)
disadvantages: The body still accepts FOUNDER_TIER and a first_founder_body designation from a rehearsal key
The variable covers only the two named modules
The workflow has never run on GitHub Actions
One founder-signed MISSION opening with [REHEARSAL] holds the whole body below the tier, retroactively
alternatives.revival_evidence: Retained as proposed. Revisit when #221 lands (write-side refusal) or the workflow's first run reports.

alternatives.name: Simplest viable: put supervisord on PATH in CI and document the rehearsal key's limit
alternatives.description: Set PATH wherever the rehearsals must run, and add a sentence to greg/README.md that a rehearsal key must never attest. No code.
advantages: No code and no new surface
With supervisord on PATH the rehearsals already pass (4 passed in 129.7 s at round 1)
disadvantages: A run without PATH set still reads '4 skipped' with exit 0: nothing fails closed
A rehearsal body's own key can still move achieved to N1, the failure the 2026-10-30 intent names
A sentence is a claim, not a check (directive section 56)
alternatives.revival_evidence: Only if both the skip and the tier read were already enforced elsewhere.

alternatives.name: Strongest competing: refuse at write time in greg/body.py, plus a suite-wide fail-on-skip
alternatives.description: The spec's full form: the body refuses FOUNDER_TIER and BODY_DESIGNATE purpose=first_founder_body from a rehearsal body, so the attestation never enters the ledger. A pytest policy turns every skip into a failure in CI.
advantages: No reader has to know about rehearsals: the attestation is never written
Also closes the designation path; greg acceptance's FOUNDER-DEVICE label reads the designation, not the mark
disadvantages: greg/body.py is edited by open #221 and #235
Rehearsal bodies already made hold their attestations in their ledgers; a read-side check is still needed for them
A suite-wide fail-on-skip turns legitimately optional skips (Landlock, bubblewrap, browsers) into failures on hosts without them
alternatives.revival_evidence: #221 lands; the write-side refusal is then the named follow-up, with fail-before tests and mutants.

alternatives.name: Staged experiment: the workflow alone first
alternatives.description: Land build-frontier.yml running both gates and the rehearsals with supervisord on PATH, watch its first runs, then decide on metrics.
advantages: Smallest diff; reversible by deleting one file
Gives the first real CI timings before more code
disadvantages: Leaves the founder-tier path open while later nodes are built on rehearsal bodies
Without the helper, a runner missing supervisord still reads skipped
alternatives.revival_evidence: Adopted in part: the workflow is in this change and can be removed alone; its first run is a review trigger.
